_comment: The centre column is the instrument. A seismometer works because its mass does NOT move with the
ground -- decouple it from the frame or it rides along and records nothing -- so the astrite hangs
from the chain, and the clock beneath it turns the drum. That is why the mass is astrite rather than
any dense thing: it is the one material in the pack that is not of any Age, which is exactly the
property the physics asks for. The ink beside it inks the stylus; the paper beside the clock is what
A SHARD and not a block (Jonah, 2026-09-07). A block was argued for on heft and refused on economy:
astrite's bulk already goes into blocks, for the golem and for the lure, so an instrument taking one
too would leave the shard as nothing but an intermediate. Its direct uses are what keep it a material.
Deliberately lighter than the geologist's tools, and the pair divides by ERA rather than by cost. The
tools span the vanilla worlds -- Nether, deep dark, a geode, a diamond, a lodestone -- and are the
early instrument. This one gates on a written Age survived: one unassuming shard carries a meteoric
Age and a storm caught or a crater hunted, which is why the list reads cheaper than the instrument is.
